_comment: 'fp' is the ROOT of the identity: memoryType 'sp' (Table 43), secret,
obscured, never sent on the bus. In a product it would be factory-written
to a secure element; here the file stands in for that. It must be a 256-bit
TRUE RANDOM number, and it is also the seed the gateway's signing key pair
is derived from -- which is what makes the public ID verifiable.
'pi' (Table 41, 'ro') is DERIVED from 'fp', not provisioned: it is the X
coordinate of that key pair's public point, 64 hex characters. It is public
and STATIONARY -- the same for the life of the gateway, because the
Stating 'pi' here is OPTIONAL, but if you do it must equal the derived
value or the gateway refuses to start. The derived value is logged at
startup (it is public), so it can be pasted in from there.
The 'pi' below IS that derived value for the 'fp' above. Keeping it here
documents what the derivation produces AND pins it: if the KDF salt or
info string ever changes, this fixture fails loudly instead of silently
giving every gateway a different public ID.
These are DEMO values, not real secrets. For a real one, paste in your own
64 hex characters for 'fp' (e.g. openssl rand -hex 32), then chmod 600.
